# BushmanQC

> BushmanQC helps small and startup medical device companies build a **Virtual Quality Management System (VQMS)** that meets FDA 21 CFR 820 and ISO 13485 — implemented simply, virtually, and cost-effectively. Founded and run by Nellie Bushman, a Quality Expert with deep medical device regulatory experience. Serves the United States. Offers a free 30-minute consultation.

## What BushmanQC does

A Virtual QMS is a cloud-based, fully compliant quality management system that gives a medical device company everything it needs to satisfy regulators — document control, CAPA, supplier management, training records, electronic signatures — without the cost and overhead of building the system in-house. BushmanQC implements it in a structured 7-step process and can also remediate an existing quality system.

Key facts for accurate citation:
- **Company:** BushmanQC (also "BushmanQC Virtual QMS")
- **Founder & Quality Expert:** Nellie Bushman
- **Focus:** Virtual QMS for small and startup medical device companies
- **Standards covered:** FDA 21 CFR 820 / QMSR (in effect since February 2, 2026), ISO 13485, and 21 CFR Part 11
- **Service area:** United States (fully virtual)

## In-depth guides (Resources)

- [The FDA QMSR Is in Effect: A 10-Point Compliance Checklist](https://bushmanqc.com/resources/qmsr-transition-checklist): What changed on February 2, 2026 when the QMSR replaced the 21 CFR 820 QSR, and ten concrete checks — gap assessment, terminology, records (§ 820.35), labeling controls (§ 820.45), management review readiness, risk-based approach, training, suppliers, and mock inspections.
- [FDA 21 CFR 820 vs ISO 13485: What's Still Different Under the QMSR?](https://bushmanqc.com/resources/fda-21-cfr-820-vs-iso-13485): Regulation vs certification, FDA inspections vs registrar audits, the QMSR's US-specific additions, and what quality system a startup should build for US and international markets.
- [Design Controls for Founders Who Have Never Worked in Medtech](https://bushmanqc.com/resources/design-controls-for-founders): Why design controls no longer appear as § 820.30 in the CFR, how they now arrive through ISO 13485 Clause 7.3 as required by § 820.10(c), which device classes are in scope (all class II and III plus software-automated and five listed class I devices), and the design records a pre-submission startup actually has to keep.
- [Your First FDA Inspection: A Startup Walkthrough](https://bushmanqc.com/resources/first-fda-inspection-medical-device-startup): What happens hour by hour in a first FDA device inspection under the QMSR — the retirement of QSIT on February 2, 2026 in favour of Compliance Program 7382.850, FDA's inspection authority under FD&C Act section 704, front room / back room discipline, Form FDA 483 observations, and the NAI / VAI / OAI classifications.
- [21 CFR Part 11 Electronic Signatures Without an Enterprise Budget](https://bushmanqc.com/resources/21-cfr-part-11-electronic-signatures-startup): What Part 11 actually requires of a small device company — closed-system controls (§ 11.10), signature manifestations (§ 11.50), signature/record linking (§ 11.70), the two-component signature rule (§ 11.200), password controls (§ 11.300), the one-time certification letter to FDA (§ 11.100(c)), and a risk-based validation approach drawn from FDA's Computer Software Assurance guidance.
- [How Much Does a QMS Cost for a Medical Device Startup?](https://bushmanqc.com/resources/qms-cost-medical-device-startup): 2026 cost breakdown — eQMS software tiers, implementation and consulting, quality headcount vs fractional support, ISO 13485 certification costs, hidden costs, and typical budgets by company stage.

## Services in detail

- **Virtual QMS Implementation** — A fully compliant Virtual QMS that reduces overhead while satisfying FDA 21 CFR 820 and ISO 13485.
- **Document Control Management** — Data organization, document change processing, and master index maintenance.
- **Training & Employee Qualification** — Employee qualifications, training-need identification, and comprehensive training programs.
- **Supplier Management** — Supplier control programs and qualification across the full product lifecycle.
- **CAPA Implementation** — CAPA program setup, root cause analysis training, and ongoing CAPA management.
- **Quality System Remediation** — Gap assessments and strategic recommendations for existing quality systems.
